seo.line: An SEO title and an SEO description for every page and post, in the editor's sidebar.

page.seo_title: Mody SEO: a free, simple SEO plugin for WordPress | Mody Cloud
page.seo_description: Mody SEO gives every page and post an SEO title and description in the editor's sidebar. Free (GPL), for single sites and multisites, no outside calls.
page.lead: Choose how each page and post shows in search results: an SEO title and an SEO description, written in the editor's sidebar.
page.problem_heading: Search results show what WordPress guesses
problem: Out of the box, WordPress makes each page's title from its name and your site's, and prints no description at all. Search engines then pick a snippet of the page themselves.
Larger SEO plugins add many screens, scores and settings. Mody SEO does one thing: it lets you write the two lines people read before they click.
page.features_heading: Two fields, in the place you already work

features.title: In the editor's sidebar
features.text: The Search engines panel sits in the document sidebar of the post editor and the Site Editor. Type an SEO title and an SEO description, see their length as you go, and save them with the page.

features.title: Sensible when empty
features.text: Leave a field empty and WordPress's own title is used ("Page title – Site"), and the page's excerpt becomes its description. The panel shows in grey what will be used.

features.title: One clean head
features.text: The SEO title becomes the page's whole title tag, and the description one meta description tag, cut at 160 characters at a word. Password-protected pages get no description.

features.title: Light on your database
features.text: Two post meta fields on pages, posts and the other public post types. No settings screen and no tables of its own. If WordPress's AI plugin is there, its own description gives way, so a page has one.

calls.title: Nothing while it works
calls.text: No outside service, no score computed elsewhere, no ping to search engines, no script or font from a CDN. Your titles and descriptions stay in your own database.

calls.title: mody.cloud, for updates
calls.text: At most twice a day it asks mody.cloud whether a newer version exists, so WordPress can show its usual update notice. The request carries nothing about your site: no address, no version.

calls.title: Where that request goes
calls.text: mody.cloud runs on our own server in Spain. While Mody Cloud is small, Cloudflare, a US company, sits in front of it and sees that request; we will replace it as soon as we can.

Open a page in the editor: the Search engines panel is in the sidebar.
page.mody_heading: Built into every Mody Cloud site
page.mody_text: On Mody Cloud, Mody SEO is already on, and Mody, your site's AI agent, writes the SEO title and description for you when you ask. Free: one site, no card, for people who live in Spain.

faq.q: Does it make a sitemap or add Open Graph tags?
faq.a: No. WordPress already makes a sitemap (wp-sitemap.xml). Mody SEO does not print Open Graph or Twitter tags yet, so link previews on social networks are left to WordPress and the network.

faq.q: Does it give my pages a score?
faq.a: No. There are no keyphrases, scores or traffic lights. Write the two lines for people: search results show about 60 characters of a title, and descriptions of 70 to 160 characters work best.

faq.q: What about categories, tags and archives?
faq.a: They keep WordPress's own title and get no description. Mody SEO covers pages, posts and the other public post types.

faq.q: Can I use it next to another SEO plugin?
faq.a: Better not: both would print a title and a description. Choose one.

faq.q: What happens if I remove it?
faq.a: Your pages keep their content. The two fields stay in the database and are simply no longer printed, so WordPress's own title comes back.

faq.q: Where do I report a problem or ask for help?
faq.a: Open an issue in our code repository on GitHub, with the link at the bottom of this page. We plan to move our code to Codeberg, a European home for open source.

faq.q: Is it really free?
faq.a: Yes. It is free software under the GPL (version 2 or later): use it, change it and share it, on as many sites as you like.

page.seo_title: Mody Security: free two-step login and firewall for WordPress | Mody Cloud
page.seo_description: Two-step login with an app or a security key, login limits, a firewall, a file check and a security log. Free (GPL), with no outside security service.
page.lead: Protect your logins and your site with code that runs on your own server: two-step login with an app or a security key, login limits, a firewall, a file check, a security log and alerts.
facts: Two-step login with an app or a key
page.problem_heading: Security should not depend on someone else's servers
problem: Many security plugins check logins, visitors' addresses or your files against their company's servers, and keep part of their protection for a paid plan.
Mody Security does the work on your own server. It is the code that protects every Mody Cloud site, free and the same for everyone.
page.features_heading: Logins, requests and files, watched from your server

features.title: Two-step login
features.text: After the password, a six-digit code from an authenticator app, or a security key or passkey. Ten recovery codes for a lost phone. Administrators must use it by default; you choose who.

features.title: Login protection
features.text: Limits per address and per account pause password guessing, and usernames such as admin or root can never log in. ALTCHA, a puzzle the visitor's browser solves and your server checks, guards login, lost password and comments.

features.title: A firewall
features.text: Our own rules look at the address asked for and at form data for SQL injection, script injection, path tricks and PHP code. Add addresses to block, or to always allow.

features.title: A file check
features.text: It finds scripts in the uploads folder. Write a list of your code once (wp mody-security files-manifest), and it also finds every changed, added or missing file in WordPress, plugins and themes.

features.title: A log and alerts
features.text: Logins, failed attempts, paused addresses and blocks, kept 30 days. Emails you choose: an administrator logging in from a new browser, an address paused, files changed, a firewall block.

calls.title: Nothing while it works
calls.text: No security service, no list downloaded from a company, no CAPTCHA from another site: ALTCHA's puzzle is made and checked by your own server, and the log stays in your database.

calls.title: mody.cloud, for updates
calls.text: At most twice a day it asks mody.cloud whether a newer version exists, so WordPress can show its usual update notice. The request carries nothing about your site: no address, no version.

calls.title: Where that request goes
calls.text: mody.cloud runs on our own server in Spain. While Mody Cloud is small, Cloudflare, a US company, sits in front of it and sees that request; we will replace it as soon as we can.

In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the zip, then Install Now and Activate.
WordPress then sends you to your profile to set up two-step login. Save the recovery codes, then open Settings → Security.
page.mody_heading: Built into every Mody Cloud site
page.mody_text: On Mody Cloud, Mody Security protects every site and its login page, with nothing for you to set up. Free: one site, no card, for people who live in Spain.

faq.q: Can it lock me out?
faq.a: After activation, administrators set up two-step login before anything else, and get ten recovery codes. If you lose your phone, your keys and your codes, WP-CLI turns it off for one account: wp mody-security two-factor reset <user>.

faq.q: Do application passwords and WP-CLI need the second step?
faq.a: No. Application passwords and WP-CLI work as WordPress expects. Keep application passwords secret, as you keep your password.

faq.q: Does it slow my site down?
faq.a: The firewall reads each request's address and form data with a few patterns before WordPress does the rest. The file check runs only when you ask for it.

faq.q: Can I use it next to another security plugin?
faq.a: Better not: two plugins guarding the same login would ask twice and could block each other.

faq.q: Where do I report a problem or ask for help?
faq.a: Open an issue in our code repository on GitHub, with the link at the bottom of this page. We plan to move our code to Codeberg, a European home for open source.

faq.q: Is it really free?
faq.a: Yes. It is free software under the GPL (version 2 or later): use it, change it and share it, on as many sites as you like.

page.seo_description: Count visits and page views on your own server: no cookies, nothing stored in the browser, no address kept. Free (GPL), for single sites and multisites.
page.lead: Know how many people read your site, which pages they open and in what order, with no cookie, nothing stored in their browser and no address kept.
page.problem_heading: Most analytics send your visitors elsewhere
problem: The usual analytics load a script from another company and send it every visit, with the visitor's address and a cookie that follows them. Then the site needs a cookie banner.
Mody Analytics counts on your own server. It keeps patterns, not people: a visitor is a random visit that is forgotten the next day.

features.title: No cookie, no address
features.text: A few lines of script send one small beacon per page to your own site. A visitor is recognised for one day by a hash with a salt that changes daily; then the hash is deleted. No address is kept.

features.title: Visits and journeys
features.text: Each page view is stored under a random visit: the page, where the visit came from (direct, search, social or another site) and the device. A visit ends after 30 minutes without a new page.

features.title: Country and city, if you want them
features.text: Put DB-IP's free City Lite file on your server and Mody Analytics adds the country and city of each view, looked up locally. A city with fewer than five visits shows only as its country.

features.title: Kept for 13 months
features.text: Page views are kept 13 months, then reduced to daily totals. Logged-in users count too, anonymously; bots do not.

calls.title: Nothing while it counts
calls.text: The beacon goes to your own site, the numbers stay in your database, and the location file, if you add one, is read on your server. No script or pixel from another company.

page.problem_heading: Phone pictures are heavy, and they say where you were
problem: A photo from a phone is often 4,000 pixels wide and several megabytes, and it carries the place it was taken. WordPress keeps that original, makes a copy, and your pages load slowly.
Image services fix it by sending your pictures to their servers. Mody Images does it on your own server, when you upload.
page.features_heading: Light pictures, with nothing to set

features.title: WebP, sized for the web
features.text: JPEG, PNG and HEIC become WebP, at most 2560 pixels on a side (quality 82 for photos, 90 for PNG), and every size WordPress makes is WebP too. No -scaled copy, no heavy original kept.

features.title: Upright and private
features.text: Pictures are turned the way the camera held them, and their EXIF, XMP and IPTC data, the place included, are removed. The color profile is kept.

features.title: Left alone when they should be
features.text: GIF, SVG and animations are never touched, and WebP or AVIF files are changed only when they are larger than 2560 pixels.

features.title: Older pictures too
features.text: wp mody-images optimize converts the media library you already have, and rewrites the addresses in your content. Back up first: the old files are deleted.

calls.title: Nothing while it works
calls.text: Pictures are converted on your server with Imagick, or GD without it. Nothing is uploaded to an image service or a CDN.

features.text: A Mody fonts tab in Editor → Styles → Typography → Manage fonts. Install a family, then choose it for your text, headings or buttons.

features.title: No Google Fonts

calls.title: Nothing at all
calls.text: The font files are inside the plugin. Installing one copies it into your site's fonts folder; visitors load it from your site.
